title: sprites.json roster has three unenforced homes — texture/bbox pairing silently breaks on regeneration
detail: Textures pair with the hardcoded files array, bboxes with the JSON order array, indices via scattered constants — never reconciled. A regenerated order (the documented 6-type roster) silently mis-crops sprites; the structure and value-range checks pass.
recommended_fix: Parse the sidecar first and drive texture loads from order[i] (or assert files[i]==order[i] and fail the sheet); name the sprite indices via one constant table; read `res` instead of hardcoding 256.

title: palcheck hand-restates the camera transform — a third copy of the fit/offset math
evidence:
harness/palcheck.odin:212-215 (the zoomed-lane canary):
		view.scale *= 2.6
		view.off_x = f32(view.win_w) / 2 - f32(8) * view.tile_px * view.scale
		view.off_y = f32(view.win_h) / 2 - f32(15) * view.tile_px * view.scale
		view.lane_detail = true

app/main.odin:1199-1202 (camera_update — the canon it imitates):
	v.scale = fit * app.cam_zoom
	v.off_x = f32(v.win_w)/2 - app.cam_wx * v.scale
	v.off_y = f32(v.win_h)/2 - app.cam_wy * v.scale
	v.lane_detail = app.cam_zoom > 1.5
detail: The zoomed-lane canary needs the app's zoomed read, but the camera model is app-private, so palcheck re-implements scale/off/lane_detail. A future camera-model change silently stops the canary representing the app's real zoomed frame.
recommended_fix: Extract a pure render-side proc (e.g. camera_apply(v, wx, wy, zoom)) that camera_update and palcheck both call — the transform and the 1.5x lane threshold live once.

title: palcheck's file-scope `fails` mutable is the repo's only package-level global, against ODN-13 and the harness's own pattern
detail: Every other harness check threads failure state as a parameter; this is the sole mutable package-level variable in the codebase, diverging from ODN-13's no-globals conduct and the local check_golden precedent.
recommended_fix: Thread a ^int (or return a fail count) through check/run_palcheck the way check_golden does; delete the package-level var.
